summary.text: 唱 is traditionally analyzed as 口, marking the vocal meaning category, plus 昌, which provides a sound cue. It commonly means “sing” or “chant”; an older gloss also gives “lead” or “guide.”

formation.text: 唱 is a phonosemantic compound: 口 marks the vocal meaning category, and 昌 supplies the sound. 字源 proposes that 昌 was an earlier graph for the word later written 唱, with 口 added to form 唱; this proposed sequence is not established.

components.text: 口 marks the vocal meaning category in 唱. No distinct earlier form for this component within 唱 is established.
昌 serves as the phonetic component in 唱. 字源 proposes 昌 as an earlier graph for the word later written 唱, but this does not establish the compound’s graphic chronology.

sound.text: Zhengzhang reconstructs 昌 and 唱 with the same initial and rhyme, while the final -s marks a difference in the reconstructed form. These are system-specific reconstructions, not recorded ancient pronunciations.

The Guangyun categories show related initials and rhyme categories but different tones: 昌 is level-tone and 唱 departing-tone. This supports the traditional sound analysis but does not record pronunciation at formation.
sound.component_reading: level tone, 陽 rhyme, open division III (fanqie 尺良)
sound.character_reading: departing tone, 漾 rhyme, open division III (fanqie 尺亮)

sound.text: In present-day Mandarin, 昌 is chāng and 唱 is chàng; the tone differs. This modern comparison does not establish their historical phonetic relationship.

history.text: 唱 is analyzed as 口 plus phonetic 昌. 字源 proposes that 昌 was an earlier graph for the word and that adding 口 formed 唱; no dated sequence establishes when the written compound appeared.
Older texts are reported to have often used 倡 for 唱. 倡 is a related graph formed with 人 and phonetic 昌, not an earlier graphic form of 唱.

uncertainties.text: 字源 proposes a relationship between the earlier graph 昌 and the word later written 唱, but the available evidence does not establish when the compound graph appeared or a dated sequence of its graphic development. No corruption within 唱 is established. The reported seal-style image is a modern redraw, not an artifact image.

senses.text: A traditional gloss gives “lead or guide”; a cited example describes the yu leading while the other instruments follow. The sources do not establish that this is the earliest attested sense.
唱 commonly means “sing” or “chant” in present-day use; dictionaries also report older examples. The cited evidence does not establish when this use began or its chronology relative to “lead.”
Calling or shouting is reported in cited examples, but its chronology and relation to the other meanings are unresolved.
A cited historical example uses 唱 as a noun meaning “song” or “tune.” The available evidence does not establish when this use began or its relationship to other meanings.
